trygetnonenumeratedcount.title: Get a sequence count without forcing enumeration
trygetnonenumeratedcount.short: Ask whether a count is cheaply available before enumerating.
trygetnonenumeratedcount.summary: TryGetNonEnumeratedCount obtains the count from supported sequence shapes without walking the sequence. It reports false when the count cannot be determined cheaply.
trygetnonenumeratedcount.why: Calling Count can execute an iterator or query just to learn its size.
trygetnonenumeratedcount.tips: Treat false as a normal result and enumerate only when the count is actually required.

collections-marshal-value-ref.title: Update Dictionary values by reference with CollectionsMarshal
collections-marshal-value-ref.short: Avoid a second dictionary lookup on measured hot paths.
collections-marshal-value-ref.summary: CollectionsMarshal.GetValueRefOrAddDefault returns a reference to a Dictionary value slot, allowing an existing value to be updated in place or a default slot to be initialized.
collections-marshal-value-ref.why: It can avoid repeated hashing and lookups in performance-sensitive dictionary update loops.
collections-marshal-value-ref.tips: The returned reference can be invalidated by dictionary mutations; keep its lifetime short and prefer ordinary Dictionary APIs unless measurements justify this lower-level API.

taskcompletionsource-runasync.title: Run TaskCompletionSource continuations asynchronously
taskcompletionsource-runasync.short: Avoid unexpectedly running await continuations inside SetResult.
taskcompletionsource-runasync.summary: TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously asks TaskCompletionSource to schedule continuations instead of allowing them to execute inline on the thread that completes the task.
taskcompletionsource-runasync.why: Inline continuations can unexpectedly extend a lock or callback path and create reentrancy or deadlock risks.
taskcompletionsource-runasync.tips: This option is a useful default when adapting callback-style APIs, but still design completion and cancellation races explicitly.

async-enumerable-withcancellation.title: Cancel await foreach with WithCancellation
async-enumerable-withcancellation.short: Pass a CancellationToken into asynchronous enumeration.
async-enumerable-withcancellation.summary: WithCancellation attaches a CancellationToken to consumption of an IAsyncEnumerable<T> so a cancellable iterator can observe cancellation while await foreach advances it.
async-enumerable-withcancellation.why: A token available to the caller does nothing unless it is propagated into the asynchronous enumeration.
async-enumerable-withcancellation.tips: The iterator must cooperate with cancellation; for iterator methods, CancellationToken parameters commonly use EnumeratorCancellation.

convert-tryfrombase64string.title: Decode Base64 into an existing buffer
convert-tryfrombase64string.short: Use TryFromBase64String when you want span-based decoding.
convert-tryfrombase64string.summary: Convert.TryFromBase64String attempts to decode text directly into a destination Span<byte> and reports how many bytes were written.
convert-tryfrombase64string.why: It avoids creating a decoded byte array when the caller already owns suitable storage.
convert-tryfrombase64string.tips: Size the destination for the maximum decoded length and handle false for invalid input or insufficient space.

sequenceequal-span-comparison.title: Compare spans with SequenceEqual
sequenceequal-span-comparison.short: Compare contiguous sequences without converting them first.
sequenceequal-span-comparison.summary: Span and ReadOnlySpan support SequenceEqual for element-by-element equality, which is useful for binary signatures and slices.
sequenceequal-span-comparison.why: Converting slices to arrays or strings just for equality creates unnecessary temporary objects.
sequenceequal-span-comparison.tips: For text, choose comparison semantics deliberately; SequenceEqual is an ordinal element comparison, not culture-aware text comparison.

dictionary-ensure-capacity.title: Pre-size Dictionary with EnsureCapacity
dictionary-ensure-capacity.short: Reserve capacity when the expected entry count is known.
dictionary-ensure-capacity.summary: Dictionary.EnsureCapacity makes room for at least the requested number of entries without changing existing key-value pairs.
dictionary-ensure-capacity.why: Known large insert batches can otherwise trigger repeated internal growth and rehashing.
dictionary-ensure-capacity.tips: Use realistic estimates; excessive preallocation wastes memory and is rarely useful for small dictionaries.

gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.title: Use AllocateUninitializedArray only when every element will be overwritten
gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.short: Skip zero initialization for measured full-overwrite array workloads.
gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.summary: GC.AllocateUninitializedArray<T> can allocate an array without guaranteeing zero-initialized contents, intended for cases that immediately overwrite every element.
gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.why: For large arrays on hot paths, skipping initialization can remove work that would immediately be discarded.
gc-allocate-uninitialized-array.tips: Never read an element before writing it, and prefer normal arrays unless profiling shows initialization cost matters.

stream-copytoasync.title: Copy streams asynchronously with CopyToAsync
stream-copytoasync.short: Use the built-in buffered stream copy operation.
stream-copytoasync.summary: Stream.CopyToAsync reads from one stream and writes to another asynchronously until the source reaches its end.
stream-copytoasync.why: It avoids hand-written read/write loops when the task is simply to copy all remaining bytes.
stream-copytoasync.tips: Pass a CancellationToken when cancellation matters and remember that disposing the streams remains the caller's responsibility.

cancellationtokensource-cancelafter.title: Apply a timeout with CancellationTokenSource.CancelAfter
cancellationtokensource-cancelafter.short: Schedule cancellation after a duration while preserving caller cancellation.
cancellationtokensource-cancelafter.summary: CancelAfter schedules a CancellationTokenSource to become canceled after a delay. A linked source can combine that timeout with an existing caller token.
cancellationtokensource-cancelafter.why: It gives operations that already accept CancellationToken a consistent timeout signal without separate timer plumbing.
cancellationtokensource-cancelafter.tips: Dispose linked sources, distinguish timeout from caller cancellation when the application needs different handling, and use Task.WaitAsync when you only need to limit how long the caller waits.
